revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Wiring the Studio
revealWordProblem.text: A recording studio runs cables for its microphones. The cost of wiring one room is the expression 5x + 7 + 3x + 2, where x is the number of microphones in that room. Write the cost as a simplified expression by combining like terms. Then find the total cost when the room has x = 4 microphones.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Combine like terms: 5x + 3x = 8x and 7 + 2 = 9, so the simplified expression is 8x + 9. When x = 4, the cost is 8(4) + 9 = 32 + 9 = 41 dollars.

vocabulary.definition: You can change the order and get the same answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Puedes cambiar el orden y obtener la misma respuesta.
vocabulary.visual: 3 + 7 = 7 + 3 = 10 both ways; 4 × 5 = 5 × 4 = 20 both ways — order does not matter
vocabulary.cloze: The rule that order does not change a sum or product, like a + b = b + a, is the ___.

examples.why: Changing the order keeps the same sum.
That shows the associative property, which regroups.

vocabulary.definition: You can change the grouping and get the same answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Puedes cambiar la agrupación y obtener la misma respuesta.
vocabulary.cloze: The rule that grouping does not change a sum or product, like (a + b) + c = a + (b + c), is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: Multiplying a number by everything inside the parentheses: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar un número por todo lo que está dentro del paréntesis: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
vocabulary.visual: 3(4 + 5) = 3×4 + 3×5 = 12 + 15 = 27 — the 3 gets 'distributed' to both the 4 and the 5
vocabulary.cloze: The rule that a(b + c) = ab + ac is the ___.

examples.why: The 3 is multiplied by each term inside.

vocabulary.definition: A factor of a whole number divides it evenly, with no remainder. For example, 3 is a factor of 12 because 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un factor de un número entero lo divide exactamente, sin dejar residuo. Por ejemplo, 3 es un factor de 12 porque 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
vocabulary.visual: In 3(x + 2), the 3 is the factor outside the parentheses that multiplies each term inside
vocabulary.cloze: To rewrite a sum as a product, like 3x + 12 = 3(x + 4), is to ___.

vocabulary.definition: Expressions that always have the same value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresiones que siempre tienen el mismo valor.
vocabulary.visual: 2x + 4 and 2(x + 2): when x = 3, both = 10; when x = 7, both = 18 — always the same

vocabulary.definition: To write an expression in a shorter, simpler way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una expresión de forma más corta y simple.
vocabulary.visual: 3x + 2x + 5 simplifies to 5x + 5 — fewer terms, same value
vocabulary.cloze: To write an expression in its shortest equal form is to ___ it.

vocabulary.definition: Terms with the same letter raised to the same power, like 2x and 5x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Términos con la misma letra elevada a la misma potencia, como 2x y 5x.
vocabulary.visual: 5x and 3x are like terms (both x); 5x and 5y are NOT (different variables); 2x and 2x² are NOT (different powers)
vocabulary.cloze: Terms with the same variable part, like 3y and 8y, are ___.

examples.why: They share the same variable y.
They have different variables, so they are not like terms.

vocabulary.definition: To add or subtract terms with the same letter into one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar o restar términos con la misma letra en uno solo.
vocabulary.visual: 8m + 3m = 11m — add the coefficients (8 + 3 = 11) and keep the variable (m)
vocabulary.cloze: To add or subtract like terms into a single term is to ___ them.

launch.narrative: Missed a lesson — or just want a refresher? This catch-up station reviews Lessons 6.4–6.7: 6.4 Properties of Operations, 6.5 The Distributive Property, 6.6 Equivalent Expressions, 6.7 Simplify Algebraic Expressions. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 6.4–6.7
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 6.4: Changing the order or the grouping of numbers being added or multiplied does not change the answer. • 6.5: The number outside the parentheses gets "shared" with every term inside. • 6.6: Equivalent expressions give the same answer for every value of the variable. • 6.7: Only combine terms that have the same variable part; numbers without a variable combine with each other.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 6.4 — Properties of Operations: Changing the order or the grouping of numbers being added or multiplied does not change the answer.
Lesson 6.5 — The Distributive Property: The number outside the parentheses gets "shared" with every term inside.
Lesson 6.6 — Equivalent Expressions: Equivalent expressions give the same answer for every value of the variable.
Lesson 6.7 — Simplify Algebraic Expressions: Only combine terms that have the same variable part; numbers without a variable combine with each other.

Stuck on one lesson's problems? Open that lesson from the curriculum menu for the full re-teach.

explore.instructions: Identify the like terms in each expression. Group the terms that can be combined.

discourse.prompt: What rule determines whether two terms are 'like terms'? Why can't you combine unlike terms?
discourse.sentenceFrame: Two terms are like terms when they have the same ___. You cannot combine ___ and ___ because they represent different ___.

optional.stem: (Lesson 6.4) Track 2 on the playlist plays 5(7 + 2) = 5 × 7 + 5 × 2. Which property is this?
optional.explanation: Multiplying 5 across both numbers inside the parentheses (5 × 7 and 5 × 2) shows the Distributive Property.
choiceFeedback: Associative is about grouping (parentheses), Commutative is about order.

optional.stem: (Lesson 6.5) Light Cue 1: Expand 3(x + 4) for the stage-light controller.
optional.explanation: Distribute the 3 to each term: 3 × x + 3 × 4 = 3x + 12.
choiceFeedback: You added 3 + 4 first, but you need to multiply 3 by each term.

optional.stem: (Lesson 6.6) Producer A wrote 2(x + 3) for a beat's cost. Which expression is equivalent?
optional.explanation: Distribute the 2 to each term inside: 2 · x + 2 · 3 = 2x + 6. Check x = 5: 2(5 + 3) = 16 and 2(5) + 6 = 16.
choiceFeedback: Adding 2 + 3 first doesn't match the property. Distribute the 2.
Multiply 2 by x, and multiply 2 by 3, then add.

optional.stem: (Lesson 6.7) The board shows 3x + 5x on one channel. Simplify it.
optional.explanation: 3x and 5x are like terms, so add the coefficients: 3 + 5 = 8. The variable x stays, giving 8x.
choiceFeedback: 3x and 5x are like terms. Add the coefficients: 3 + 5 = 8. Result: 8x.
Did you multiply 3 × 5? You're adding like terms, not multiplying.
Both have x, so combine: 3x + 5x = 8x.

approaching.explanation: The order of the addends changed, so this is the Commutative Property of Addition.
choiceFeedback: Associative changes the grouping, not the order. Commutative swaps positions.
5 and 13 switched sides: 5 + 13 = 13 + 5. That's Commutative.
hints: Compare the two sides: same numbers, same operation. What changed between left and right?
Match the change to the property: order swapping, regrouping with parentheses, or adding 0 / multiplying by 1.
Left is 5 + 13; right is 13 + 5. The addends traded places — find the property about changing order.

approaching.explanation: The grouping (parentheses) changed but the order stayed the same, so this is the Associative Property of Multiplication.
choiceFeedback: Only the parentheses moved. That's Associative, not Commutative (which swaps order).
The grouping changed from (6 × 3) × 2 to 6 × (3 × 2). That's Associative.
hints: Read both sides carefully: 6, 3, 2 stay in the same order. Only the parentheses moved.
Ask: did the ORDER change, or did the GROUPING change? Each property handles one of those.
Left groups (6 × 3) first; right groups (3 × 2) first. Pick the property that's about regrouping.

choiceFeedback: Did you only multiply 6 by n? You also need 6 × 3 = 18.
Distribute 6 to both terms inside the parentheses.
hints: The 6 outside must visit BOTH terms inside the parentheses: the n and the 3.
Multiply 6 × n and 6 × 3 separately, then join the two products with the plus sign.
First product: 6 × n = 6n. Now find the second product 6 × 3 and add it on.

choiceFeedback: Distribute to both: 4 × 5 and 4 × 2, then subtract.
Even with subtraction, distribute to both terms inside.
hints: Even with subtraction inside, the 4 must multiply BOTH the 5 and the 2.
Find 4 × 5 and 4 × 2 separately, then subtract the second product from the first.
First product: 4 × 5 = 20. Next multiply 4 × 2, then subtract that product from 20.

choiceFeedback: 4x and 3x are like terms. 4x + 3x = 7x.
Combine like terms: 4 + 3 = 7, so 4x + 3x = 7x.
Both have the same variable x. Add the coefficients: 4 + 3 = 7.
hints: 4x and 3x share the exact same variable, x — that makes them like terms.
Combine like terms by adding the coefficients (the number parts). The variable tags along unchanged.
Add the coefficients: 4 + 3. Keep the x exactly as it is — no new exponent appears.

choiceFeedback: Did you forget to distribute the 2 to both terms?
2 times m is 2m, and 2 times 5 is 10.
hints: The 2 outside the parentheses must multiply both the m and the 5.
Distribute: write 2 × m and 2 × 5, then join the products with +.
Start: 2 × m = 2m. Now multiply 2 × 5 and add that product on.

choiceFeedback: 7x and 3x are like terms. 7 + 3 = 10. Result: 10x.
Did you multiply 7 × 3? Add the coefficients: 7 + 3 = 10.
Same variable x: add the coefficients 7 + 3 = 10.
hints: 7x and 3x have the same variable x, so they're like terms and can combine.
Add the coefficients; the x stays exactly the same — no squaring, no multiplying coefficients.
Compute 7 + 3 and place that sum in front of x.

approaching.explanation: 9n + 2n = 11n. The constant 4 has no like term, so it stays. Result: 11n + 4.
choiceFeedback: 9n and 2n are like terms: 9 + 2 = 11. Keep 4 separate.
4 is a constant term; 11n is the combined variable term.
hints: There are two n-terms (9n and 2n) and one lonely constant (4) with no partner.
Combine only the like terms; the constant 4 stays separate in your answer.
Add 9n + 2n by adding 9 + 2. The 4 keeps its own spot at the end.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.4) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Reasoning
workedExample.work: There are parentheses, so the grouping must have changed.

onLevel.correctWork: This is actually the Commutative Property, not the Associative Property. Look inside the parentheses: 2 + 3 became 3 + 2 — the ORDER of the addends switched, but the grouping (the parentheses) stayed in the exact same place around the first two numbers. The Associative Property would move the parentheses, like (2 + 3) + 4 = 2 + (3 + 4). Both sides still equal 9, but the property shown is commutative.
hints: Compare inside the parentheses: did the order of 2 and 3 change, or did the parentheses move to a different spot?
Associative MOVES the grouping; commutative SWITCHES the order. Which one happened here?

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 6.4) Match each equation with the property it demonstrates.
hints: These use letters, but the same clues apply: swapped order, moved parentheses, or a lone + 0 / × 1.
Scan each card for its signal: letters trading places, parentheses shifting, or a 1 or 0 doing nothing.
First card: a + b = b + a — the letters swapped order. Sort it by that clue, then find the next card's signal.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.5) Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: 5(3x + 2) = 5 × 3x + 5 × 2 = 15x + 10. The student distributed the 5 to the 3x (getting 15x) but left the 2 unchanged. The factor must multiply every term inside, so 5 × 2 = 10, not 2.
hints: The 3x became 15x — what should happen to the 2 when you multiply by 5?
The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. The 5 must reach both 3x and 2.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 6.5) Use the distributive property to expand each expression.
hints: Some inside terms have coefficients, like 2x. Multiply the outside number by the WHOLE term: 3 × 2x.
Two products per row: outside × first term, outside × second term. Keep the − sign if the inside subtracts.
Row 1: 3(2x + 5) → 3 × 2x = 6x. Now multiply 3 × 5 and join the products with +. Repeat for each row.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.6) Spot the Combining Mistake

workedExample.label: Combine
workedExample.work: Combine every number you see: 7x + 2x + 3 = 9x + 3, then add the 9 and 3 too

onLevel.correctWork: Only LIKE terms combine. 7x and 2x are like terms (7x + 2x = 9x), but the 3 is a constant and cannot be added to the 9x. The simplified form is 9x + 3. Check x = 2: 7(2) + 3 + 2(2) = 21 and 9(2) + 3 = 21, but 12(2) = 24 — so 12x is wrong.
hints: Can you add 9x and 3 into one term? Are they like terms?
Substitute x = 2 into 7x + 3 + 2x and into 12x. Do you get the same value?

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 6.6) Match each expression with its simplified form.
hints: Each card claims an expression simplifies to the given form. Verify the claim before placing it.
Redo the work yourself: combine like terms or distribute, and check both the variable part and the constant.
First card: 8y + 2y — add the coefficients 8 + 2 and see whether the result matches the card's 10y.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.7) Spot the Mistake — Swept-Up Constant
onLevel.correctWork: The 4 is a constant with no variable, so it cannot be combined with the x-terms. Combine only the like terms: 6x + 2x = 8x, and the 4 stays on its own. The correct simplified expression is 8x + 4. (Check: at x = 1, 6x + 4 + 2x = 6 + 4 + 2 = 12, and 8x + 4 = 12, but 12x = 12 only by accident — at x = 2 it gives 24 instead of the true 20.)
hints: Is 4 a like term with 6x and 2x? It has no variable, so it cannot join them.
Combine the x-terms first (6x + 2x = 8x), then write the leftover constant: 8x + 4.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 6.7) Simplify each expression by combining like terms.
hints: Row 1 shows the move: gather the matching variable terms first, then bring the constant along.
For each row, underline the variable terms and circle the constants. Combine each group separately.
Row 2: 6x + 4 + 2x + 7 — pair 6x with 2x, and 4 with 7. Add each pair, then write both parts.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.4) Find the Property Error

workedExample.label: Student's claim
workedExample.work: This shows the Commutative Property of Subtraction.

workedExample.label: Reasoning
workedExample.work: I switched the order, so it must be commutative.

extending.correctWork: 15 − 8 = 7, but 8 − 15 = −7. These are NOT equal. The commutative property does NOT apply to subtraction. It only works for addition and multiplication.
hints: Does switching the order in subtraction always give the same answer?
Try computing both sides: Is 15 − 8 the same as 8 − 15?

extending.title: (Lesson 6.5) Find the Distributive Error
extending.correctWork: 5(2x + 4) = 5 × 2x + 5 × 4 = 10x + 20. You must distribute the 5 to BOTH terms inside the parentheses, not just the first one.
hints: Did the student multiply 5 by both terms, or only the first term?
The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. Both b and c get multiplied.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.6) Find the Simplification Error
extending.correctWork: 3x + 2x = 5x (NOT 5x²). When you combine like terms, you add the coefficients, not multiply them. The correct answer is 5x + 6.
hints: When you combine 3x + 2x, do you add the exponents or the coefficients?
3x means 3 groups of x. 2x means 2 groups of x. Together that's ___ groups of x.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.7) Find the Simplification Error
extending.correctWork: 5x + 4x = 9x (like terms). 2y stays separate (no other y-term). The constant 3 stays. Correct answer: 9x + 2y + 3. You cannot combine x-terms and y-terms into xy.
hints: Can you combine 5x and 2y? Do they have the same variable?
Like terms must have the exact same variable. 5x and 4x are like terms, but 5x and 2y are not.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Simplify Algebraic Expressions is sweeping a constant into the variable terms — for example, simplifying 6x + 4 + 2x as 12x by adding all three numbers (6 + 4 + 2 = 12) instead of recognizing that 4 has no variable and cannot combine with 6x and 2x. The correct simplified expression is 8x + 4 (combine 6x + 2x = 8x, and let the 4 stay on its own). Before you submit, check that every term you combined has the exact same variable part.

diagram.title: Combining the Festival Cable Order
diagram.caption: Each row holds one type of term: add the m-parts (8+3+4=15m) and the number-parts (5+7+2=14) separately to get 15m + 14.

connect.scenario: A music festival needs supplies for 3 stages. Stage 1 needs 8m + 5 cables, Stage 2 needs 3m + 7 cables, and Stage 3 needs 4m + 2 cables, where m represents the number of microphones per stage. The total order is (8m + 5) + (3m + 7) + (4m + 2).
connect.promptQuestion: Simplify the total order expression. What does each part of the simplified expression tell you?
connect.prompt: The total order simplifies to ___m + ___. The ___ tells us ___ and the ___ tells us ___.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 6.5) Which expression is equivalent to 7(x + 3)?
exitTicket.explanation: 7(x + 3) = 7 × x + 7 × 3 = 7x + 21. The 7 must multiply BOTH terms — multiplying only the x gives 7x + 3, multiplying only the 3 gives x + 21, and adding 7 + 3 instead of multiplying gives 7x + 10.
choiceFeedback: This shows a(b + c) = ab + ac, which is the Distributive Property.
Commutative: order changes. Associative: grouping changes. Distributive: multiply across.
When multiplying across a sum or difference, that's Distributive.
hints: The 7 outside has to multiply BOTH terms inside — the x and the 3.
Form two products and join them with +. Multiplying only one of the terms is the classic trap.
First product: 7 × x = 7x. Now multiply 7 × 3 and attach that product with a plus sign before choosing.

parallelPractice.explanation: Add the x-coefficients: 6 + 4 = 10. Keep the constant term and write: 10x + 9.
